title: {name} has a family emergency
body: They are already in the car. They asked whether it was all right, which tells you what kind of place they think this is.
headline: {name} needed time off at no notice.

title: {name} is being courted
body: Word is a rival has been buying them lunch. Twice. They have not mentioned it, which is either loyalty or a decision already made.
headline: A rival has been buying {name} lunch.

title: {name} wants a raise
body: They brought numbers: three job listings, the industry survey, and the date of their last increase. None of it is wrong.
headline: {name} asked for a raise, with evidence.

strict.label: Tell them to wait for the review cycle

title: {name} wants to do a different job
body: They have been doing the other job in the evenings for two months and are better at it than the one you pay them for.
headline: {name} asked to change roles.

title: {name} and a teammate have stopped speaking
body: Nothing was said out loud. Standups run four minutes shorter and the code review queue has an obvious gap in it.
headline: {name} is routing around a teammate.

supportive.label: Sit them both down
supportive.detail: Morale +8 for everyone · an afternoon gone

title: {name} is running on fumes
body: Three commits after midnight this week. Their last message to the team channel was an apology for a typo at 2:40am.
headline: {name} has been shipping at 2am all week.

supportive.label: Take work off them for a week

title: {name} has a side project
body: It is good. It is also adjacent enough that a lawyer would have an opinion, and they built it on their own weekends.
headline: {name} has been building something on the side.

supportive.label: It's theirs — say so in writing

strict.label: Remind them of the IP clause

title: {name} wants the title
body: They have been doing the senior work for a year and watched someone else get called senior for less. They are not shouting. That is worse.
headline: {name} asked for the title they have been doing the work of.

title: {name} is having a baby
body: They want to know what the policy is. There is no policy. Whatever you say next becomes the policy.
headline: {name} asked what the parental leave policy is.

supportive.label: Full pay, three months, written down

title: {name} wants to move away
body: Their partner got a job four hours from here. They would like to keep this one. They have thought about the time zones already.
headline: {name} asked to work remotely for good.

title: {name} has made a complaint
body: It is specific, it is dated, and they have written it down. There is a right way to handle this and it is not a quiet word in the kitchen.
headline: {name} filed a formal complaint.

strict.label: Have a quiet word with everyone involved

title: {name} is leaving over the side project
body: It got an offer. They would like to build it somewhere the lawyers have not read their contract.
headline: {name} handed in notice over the side project.

strict.label: They hand in notice
strict.noticeReason: They are leaving to build the side project you said belonged to the company.

title: {name}'s side project shipped
body: It is small and it is good, and {company} is in the credits because you said it was theirs in writing. They would like to know whether you meant it.
headline: {name}'s side project shipped, with {company} in the credits.

strict.label: Ask for a share of it

title: {name} says it has happened again
body: To someone else this time. They are asking, in writing, why the first one was a quiet word in the kitchen. So is the person it happened to.
headline: A second complaint, and the first one was a quiet word.

supportive.label: Run the process now, and say why it's late

title: The process concluded
body: {name} has read the finding. They want to know whether the rest of the team will.
headline: The complaint {name} raised has a finding.

strict.label: Keep it between the people involved

title: {name} is back, and asking for four-day weeks
body: Three months went fast. They would like a four-day week until the spring, on full pay, and they are asking because the policy says nothing about it.
headline: {name} came back from leave and asked for a four-day week.

supportive.label: Four days, full pay, until spring

strict.label: Full time, or the leave was for nothing

title: {name} is not coming back
body: The statutory minimum ran out. They found somewhere with a policy.
headline: {name} did not come back from leave.

strict.label: They hand in notice
strict.noticeReason: The statutory minimum ran out, and they found somewhere with a leave policy.

title: {name} moved anyway
body: Their partner started the job. They have been doing four hours each way twice a week and they cannot keep it up. They are asking one more time.
headline: {name} moved, and asked about remote work again.

strict.label: Then this is goodbye
strict.detail: They hand in notice · team morale −3
strict.noticeReason: They moved to be with their partner, and you said this is an in-person company.

title: {name} has an offer in hand
body: The market data was right. Somebody else read it too. The number is fifteen percent over what they asked you for, and they would still rather stay.
headline: {name} came back with an offer in hand.

strict.label: Wish them luck
strict.detail: They hand in notice · team morale −5
strict.noticeReason: They took the offer you told them to wait for the review cycle over.

title: {name} is good at the new job
body: The slow start lasted a month. They are now the person the others ask. They would like the salary to notice.
headline: {name} grew into the new role.

title: {name} is still doing the other job at night
body: Two months of evenings, on somebody else's product now. They have not said so; the commits have their name on them.
headline: {name} kept doing the other job on their own time.
